Instead of retaining the parent-universe side explicitly, we describe the remaining half-geometry by a minisuperspace model with boundary conditions imposed at the throat. To model the finite throat, we introduce a small radiation component parametrized by $\epsilon$ in a closed minisuperspace model with a positive cosmological constant. The radiation term produces two turning points, an inner one $q_-\sim O(\epsilon)$ and an outer one $q_+\sim H^{-2}$, where $q$ is the square of the scale factor. Our prescription imposes the Neumann condition $\dot q(0)=0$ on the classical solutions and restricts the initial size $q_i=q(0)$ to the small-throat domain $0<|q_i|<\sqrt{\epsilon}/H$. This domain contains the inner turning point $q_-$ and excludes the unsuppressed outer-turning-point saddle at $q_i=q_+$. We choose the steepest-descent lapse contour through the inner tunneling saddle in the semiclassical approximation. Taking the limit $\epsilon\to0$ after this finite-throat saddle problem has been defined, the inner turning point approaches $q_i=0$, and the saddle action reduces to that of the standard tunneling saddle. Other choices of lapse contour can instead select Hartle-Hawking-type growing branches. In this sense, the tunneling exponent and outgoing WKB phase can be obtained as the limiting form of tunneling from an arbitrarily small universe, rather than by imposing a boundary condition directly at a vanishing geometry.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Yamada

item.title: Formation and scaling of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings for global $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2607.21701v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We numerically investigate networks of global $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings with multi-string junctions in a scalar field model whose vacuum manifold is $\mathrm{PSU}(N)=\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$. The construction of the model is motivated by the Higgs vacua of mass-deformed $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory, commonly known as $\mathcal{N}=1^*$ theory, and provides a tractable effective description of string networks with baryon-vertex-like junctions. We perform classical lattice simulations of the formation and evolution of these networks in a radiation-dominated universe. For $N=2,3,$ and $4$, the time histories suggest that the total winding-length density approaches approximate scaling over the simulated interval, with no evidence for frustration. For $N=5$ and $8$, we report densities at selected times. For the parameters studied, the density normalization grows approximately in proportion to $N^2-1$, while non-minimal-charge components remain subdominant.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Yamada

item.title: Investigating planar Proca metamaterials in nonlinear (2+1)-Electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.23013v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The present work pursues the investigation of the physics of a planar electromagnetic system incorporating nonlinear effects, as well as de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass terms in vacuum, which can be tuned to describe new planar metamaterials (MTMs) potentially suitable for technological applications. As a result, we observe interesting effects generated by a spatially dispersive profile that emerges from non-linearity. This characterizes the three-dimensional QED vacuum as a nonlocal metamaterial. The constitutive relations are derived, and the dielectric function of the metamaterial (MTM) exhibits spatial dispersion due to the Chern-Simons mass. The dispersion relations are analyzed in terms of applied external electromagnetic fields and both the de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass parameters. We also notice that, in the special case in which only a background magnetic field is present, this field gives no contribution neither to the dielectric function nor to the spatial dispersion profile, as is the case when both the electric and magnetic fields are present.
item.dc:creator: Widervan de Deus Morais, Stamatios Strikos, Ronaldo Thibes, Jos\'e Abdalla Helay\"el-Neto

item.title: CFT-Inspired Two-Horizon Thermodynamics as a Diagnostic for the Bi-Hair Organization of NUT Charge
item.description: arXiv:2607.23644v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: After decades without a fully self-consistent thermodynamic formulation, recent proposals for Lorentzian Taub-NUT spacetime have yielded several inequivalent descriptions, each satisfying its own first law and Smarr relation, leaving unresolved which formulation is physically preferred. In this Letter, we introduce a two-horizon diagnostic whose left- and right-moving thermodynamic temperatures are fixed via the harmonic mean relations before the thermodynamic variables are chosen. For uncharged Taub-NUT spacetime, the left-moving first law closes with the mass and NUT charge, whereas, within the restricted homogeneous class examined here, the right-moving first law requires an additional thermodynamic secondary hair $J_n = mn$. This result supports a bi-hair thermodynamic organization of the NUT parameter through $N = n$ and $J_n = mn$. Furthermore, this two-horizon framework offers a new opportunity toward addressing similar thermodynamic non-uniqueness in other two-horizon NUT-charged systems when the first law and Smarr relation alone do not identify a physically preferred formulation.
item.dc:creator: Di Wu, Robert B. Mann, Shuang-Qing Wu

item.title: Removability criterion for radiative corrections to the Starobinsky attractor in weakly nonlocal gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.17215v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate how the one-loop running of local couplings in weakly nonlocal, super-renormalizable completions of $R+R^{2}$ gravity affects the predictions of the Starobinsky model. Our study is motivated by the larger scalar spectral index $n_s$ preferred by recent data. For a canonical inflaton at first order in slow roll, we derive the response of the observables to an arbitrary fractional deformation $\Delta$ of the Einstein-frame potential $V$. We find that it is governed by $\mathcal{R}[\Delta]=(V/V')\Delta'$, and that the shift of the logarithm of the slow-roll parameter is twice the logarithmic derivative of the trajectory average of $\mathcal{R}$. This provides a test which requires one differentiation only. Deformations with constant $\mathcal{R}$, which we call removable, change the E-model exponent and shift $n_s$ at $O(\ln N/N^{2})$ only, where $N$ is the number of $e$-folds, while $\mathcal{R}\propto N^{k}$ gives $\Delta n_s=[2k^{2}/(k+1)]\mathcal{R}/N$. When the running is improved at the Einstein-frame Hubble rate, the renormalization-group time is half the logarithm of the tree-level potential and the gravitational flow is removable. Under a naturalness condition, a matching to the nonlocality scale yields $|\Delta n_s|\lesssim3\times10^{-4}$, a factor of about $30$ below the shift preferred by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). However, for a scale tied to the Jordan-frame curvature, the same flow is not removable and $\Delta n_s\simeq K/3$, where $K$ is a linear combination of the running parameters. Removability is a property of the flow together with the scale prescription. None of the deformations proposed since ACT DR6 that raise $n_s$ to the preferred value is removable. These results hold within a projected truncation of the local couplings and a first-order improvement of the potential.
item.dc:creator: Ekapob Kulchoakrungsun, Phongpichit Channuie, Daris Samart

item.title: Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
item.description: arXiv:2608.24791v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advancements in direct detection (DD) experiments stimulate the investigation of the interactions of dark matter (DM) with nucleons and nuclei. In the framework of Composite Higgs Models (CHMs) the lightest Dirac composite particle (LDCP) can be stable composing a significant fraction \xi of the observed DM relic abundance. We consider the elastic scattering of the LDCP on nucleons as well as on xenon (Xe) and argon (Ar) nuclei within the CHMs in which the LDCP magnetic moment, its mass and its coupling to the Higgs doublet are suppressed by an approximate U(1) symmetry. The LDCP with non-zero magnetic dipole moment can result in a substantial enhancement of the differential event rate in the DD experiments at low recoil energies of nuclei. Assuming \xi\ge 0.1, we identify the region of the parameter space where such enhancement may be potentially observable. In addition we specify some observables that can be useful in discriminating between the DM fermions with non-zero magnetic moment and other types of dark matter particles which don't have similar electromagnetic properties.
item.dc:creator: M. G. Belyakova, R. Nevzorov

item.title: Fermion mass hierarchies in a three-generation Clifford model
item.description: arXiv:2608.29259v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We examine whether an algebraic model of three fermion generations based on the complex Clifford algebra $\mathbb C\ell(10)$, in which an $S_3$ family symmetry relates the generations, can reproduce the observed mass hierarchies of the charged leptons and down quarks. Taking the internal Gram matrix as the fermion kinetic metric, we show that the original Yukawa interaction, with complex coefficients, gives precisely those ordered mass triples $0\leq m_1\leq m_2\leq m_3$ for which $m_3\leq m_1+2m_2$. This restriction excludes the observed hierarchies in both sectors and persists when the right-acting Higgs operator is allowed to range over the full Clifford algebra. This obstruction motivates a second Yukawa contraction in which a projector, constructed from the difference between an internal charge operator and its family average, acts from the left. The resulting interaction preserves the gauge and family symmetries and uses the same three Higgs doublets. With both contractions present, there is a fixed coupling ratio at which the two successive mass ratios in a single sector become arbitrarily large along a real vacuum path. Separately, a rational interval calculation establishes that one real Higgs vacuum, with different coupling ratios in the two sectors, reproduces the chosen running masses of the charged leptons and down quarks. A softly broken three-doublet potential realises this vacuum as a global minimum at tree level. The additional neutral scalars have flavour-changing couplings, and their exchange at a common mass of $2000\,\mathrm{TeV}$ satisfies the neutral-meson mixing criterion and the $\mu\to3e$ contact-interaction test considered here.
item.dc:creator: Ye Zhou, Niels Gresnigt

item.title: Covariant linear response theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2609.02615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To overcome the failure of the conventional non-relativistic description of photon statistics in strong gravitational fields and for non-comoving observers, we develop a covariant theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime, starting from the relativistic Boltzmann equation and employing the relaxation time approximation. The transport coefficients are computed up to second order in the relaxation time. The results reveal novel phenomena absent in flat space. At second order, the gravitational field renders the transport coefficients tensor-valued and induces transverse particle and energy fluxes, analogous to the Hall effect in electromagnetism. Using the first-order results, we derive the relativistic generalizations of Fick's and Fourier's laws and obtain the radiation diffusion equation for spherically symmetric accretion disks around Schwarzschild black holes. This provides a covariant description of radiative transport in strong gravitational fields for high-energy astrophysical applications.
item.dc:creator: Jianan Wang, Long Cui, Bin Wu

item.title: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
item.description: arXiv:2609.06977v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The recently discovered S301 star, with an orbital period of 8.7 years and eccentricity $e = 0.982$, reaches a pericenter of just $140\, R_{\mathrm{s}}$--- approximately nine times closer than S2's $\sim 1200R_{\mathrm{s}}$ ---offering an unprecedented laboratory for testing gravity at large post-Newtonian counting parameters. We demonstrate that S301's stellar spin precession provides a novel probe of the PPN parameter $\gamma$, scaling as $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} + 1)/3$ relative to general relativity (GR). For maximum projected velocity shifts of $46.1~{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, next-generation spectrographs could constrain $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ to $\sim10\%$ precision; this forecast is conditional on the treatment of astrophysical systematics. When combined with S301's orbital precession --- a substantial $\sim 1.95^\circ$ pericenter advance per orbit (GR prediction), approximately an order of magnitude larger than S2's $\sim 0.2^\circ$, constraining $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} - \beta_{\mathrm{PPN}}+2)/3$ --- the spin measurement breaks the $\beta$-$\gamma$ degeneracy. A projected MCMC analysis of S2 and S301 observations yields $\sigma_{2\gamma-\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ from the orbital precession and $\sigma_{\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ (with $\gamma$ fixed to its GR value by the spin measurement; $\sigma_\beta\approx0.10$ if the spin uncertainty is propagated), with the $\gamma$ precision limited by the spin precession measurement to $\sigma_{\gamma}\approx 0.1$. While the spin precession provides an independent consistency check, its true significance lies in probing the same PPN parameters at unprecedentedly large counting parameters, where the non-linear and velocity-dependent PPN terms are comparatively enhanced.

item.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
item.description: arXiv:2609.27537v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the R\'enyi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.

item.title: Relic Neutrinos Probing Small Scale Primordial Non-Gaussianity
item.description: arXiv:2609.34324v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Relic neutrinos retain a record of electromagnetic entropy production after neutrino decoupling, probing primordial modes erased from the primary CMB. We derive the cubic photon number source from acoustic damping and its leading folded sensitive bispectrum window, with neutrino decoupling, thermalization, and acoustic coherence combined in a single response kernel. For excited initial states, this kernel filters the physical folded profile and yields a sharpness dependent transmission condition, directly connecting small scale primordial non-Gaussianity to relic neutrino capture rates.
item.dc:creator: Suraj Gavhale, Shin'ichi Nojiri, Sergei D. Odintsov, Oem Trivedi

item.title: Propagation and horizon formation in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet scalar collapse. I. Characteristic conditions, bounds and formation
item.description: arXiv:2610.07166v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study scalar collapse in five- and six-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling as an exact classical theory. On spherical scalar backgrounds, gravitational characteristic conditions reduce to inequalities in two local invariants. In five dimensions, they imply $R_h^2>\tilde\alpha$ for regular marginal spheres on the GR branch and the sharp Kretschmann bound $\tilde\alpha^2\mathcal R_{abcd}\mathcal R^{abcd}<28$ for nonnegative mass. Under the stated finite-domain hypotheses, spherical continuation places the first characteristic degeneration on a smooth background. Within this setting, a future marginal sphere formed while the characteristic conditions hold throughout the preceding evolution forces their later failure. For every allowed radius, separately chosen complete smooth data form marginal spheres with mass arbitrarily close to the sharp lower bound; in six dimensions both radius and mass can be arbitrarily small. At sufficiently large scale, complete nonspherical data with weak curvature contain marginal surfaces with prescribed $S^3$ metrics under a spectral condition. These surfaces are outermost and strictly stable. A separate Berger family has arbitrarily small area at one common ADM mass; formation from untrapped data remains open. Exact nonspherical developments have smoothly convergent initial data but tidal tensors that fail to converge to the reference values at a chosen time after the reference core loses hyperbolicity. Under local geometric uniqueness for developments of the same data on overlaps connecting the initial slice to the observers, classical existence on a common region and continuous dependence of the tidal tensor cannot both hold. The constructed solutions themselves extend smoothly. Fixed time averages converge on the controlled interval, but this does not establish a predictive effective-field-theory continuation.

item.title: Fractal phase structure of QCD under imaginary rotation
item.description: arXiv:2610.07779v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that in hot QCD rotating at an imaginary angular velocity $\tilde\Omega_I$, the angular velocity selects not only the temperature of the bulk but whether charge conjugation $C$ is broken there. For QCD at temperature $T$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta$, with $\tilde\Omega_I/2\pi=p/q$ in lowest terms, the bulk far from the rotation axis is in the same thermal equilibrium state as nonrotating QCD at temperature $T/q$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta'=q\theta+\pi(p+q+1)$; this follows from the Euclidean boundary conditions and locality alone, and holds nonperturbatively whenever the equivalent nonrotating system has a finite correlation length. Consequently, even at zero quark chemical potential, the bulk is placed at the Roberge-Weiss (RW) point whenever $p$ and $q$ are both odd, and $C$ is spontaneously broken there for $T>qT_{\rm RW}$, with $T_{\rm RW}$ the RW endpoint temperature. The bulks at $\tilde\Omega_I=2\pi/3$ and $4\pi/3$, for example, are both at temperature $T/3$, yet only the former can break $C$. The set of imaginary angular velocities at which $C$ is broken has a fractal structure: raising $T$ adds rationals of ever larger denominator. At irrational $\tilde\Omega_I/2\pi$ the bulk corresponds to zero-temperature QCD at any $T$ and remains confined.

item.title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2611.18200v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arxiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arxiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arxiv:2610.22274]. This method removes the need for the freezing approximation, wherein coupling to the electromagnetic degrees of freedom are ignored, at the price of a coupled set of equations in the gravitational radiative degrees of freedom. The key insight is to transform the coupled system of equations into a chiral form which is amenable to a modified matrix $R$-separation of variables. In this work we extend the construction to the most general type D electro-vacuum solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, with aligned matter and cosmological constant. The construction makes use of the conformal properties of the equations and we find a symmetry operator underlying the decoupling of the chiral system.
item.dc:creator: Finnian Gray, Hryhorii Ovcharenko

item.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18794v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about 6.6%.
item.dc:creator: Jing Zhou, Ligong Bian

item.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
item.description: arXiv:2611.22839v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (P\'eclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e H. Gomes

item.title: A hyperbolicity obstruction near regular charged centers
item.description: arXiv:2611.24634v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A conserved charge creates a tension at a spherical center: the flux remains fixed while the area of the symmetry spheres shrinks. We ask whether curvature-dependent electromagnetic responses can reconcile bounded central curvature with hyperbolic propagation in four-dimensional Einstein gravity when both parity-even and parity-odd couplings are allowed. The background equations force a positive charge potential and its first curvature derivative to vanish at the central curvature endpoint. On branches with a positive electromagnetic kinetic coefficient and a positive effective gravitational coefficient, this endpoint flattening produces a physical extraordinary mode of the fully coupled equations whose squared angular characteristic speed is strictly below minus one at radii arbitrarily close to the center. Its characteristic cone has no hyperbolicity direction in common with the ordinary photon and graviton modes. The result requires no central curvature expansion, remains valid at points where the curvature Legendre Hessian vanishes, and extends to positive-definite mixing of finitely many Abelian fields. An exact analytic example with a nonlinear gravitational curvature sector admits a real, subluminal extraordinary photon cone near the center. In a fixed-action black-hole family, the obstruction extends outside the outer horizon over a near-extremal parameter interval.
